The surface is written principally by language models, so semantic overlap with pretraining outweighs token economy. Abbreviations do not merely fail to help, they misdirect: fx reads as audio/visual effects, dec as declare/decimal/decrement, inv as inverse. In a language where a misread clause yields a vacuous proof rather than a compile error, naming is a safety property rather than an ergonomic one. Two rules carry it: full words except where a symbol IS the concept, and every clause is a third-person-singular verb whose subject is the item, so a clause reads as a sentence with the subject elided. The evidence is already paid — a guar/ens collision consumed several design cycles in this language BECAUSE both were abbreviated.
